note: params = parameters the serving process holds after loading the model with its own inference code, before speed-ups that do not change the model (kernel fusion); every tensor counted once; LoRA counted as merged when the server merges it. Measured with bench/paramprobe (servers/start.sh). params_measured=false: still the weight-file estimate. tokenizer / max_input_tokens: the model's own tokenizer and the input limit available to our request text (history is trimmed, oldest round first, only above it).

models.params_source: servers/logs/intern-decision-0.8b.params.json (serve.py; incl. unused vision tower + projector)

models.params_source: servers/logs/bosun-0.6b.params.json (probe; base 596,038,656 + unmerged LoRA r16 10,092,544)
models.deploy_notes: Candidates follow the card's examples; authors' defaults seed=0, row_id='0' (candidate shuffle fixed per option count). No length check (base context 40960). Slower because the LoRA runs unmerged. transformers 4.57.1.

models.name: qwen3.5-0.8b-decision
models.params_source: serve.py count of the modules load() returned (Qwen3_5ForCausalLM, tied embeddings) -> servers/logs/qwen3.5-0.8b-decision.params.json
models.deploy_notes: English-only. bf16 with per-type temperatures from calibration.json. Hard cap of 52 options (A-Z, a-z). jevlite silently drops the middle of prompts above 3072 tokens; the adapter answers 422 instead, which caused the 8 failures (over-long hard long_policy items). Accuracy on the 223 answered items: 0.596; failures count as wrong.

models.name: rsi-jev-0.8b
models.params_source: launcher probe servers/logs/rsi-jev-0.8b.params.json (DecisionModel): Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base text tower incl. embeddings 752,393,024 + option_xattn scorer 7,348,225
models.deploy_notes: Authors' own server as is: tower bf16, scorer fp32. v1.0 ships no calibration file. The encoder's max_length is 2048; above it the authors' code silently cuts the state from the left instead of answering 422. 35 of the 231 public items (long_policy, multi_hop) were cut this way, so some answers come from truncated input. Served with --served-model-name rsi-jev-0.8b and --accept-model local. Option keys are visible to the model.

models.name: systemone-lite-0.5b
models.params_source: launcher probe servers/logs/systemone-lite-0.5b.params.json (Qwen2ForCausalLM, tied embeddings)
models.deploy_notes: Matches the author's self-reported 50.7%. fp16 on CUDA. Scores only the FIRST token of each option key, so keys sharing a first token get identical probabilities (in UNO: same-colour card ids tie, wild ties with wild_draw4). The request 'model' field is a model id to load; symlinks in servers/src/a-s1lite-models/ map the harness and ping names to the pinned snapshot. Input is cut at 4096 tokens on the right instead of 422; no JevBench item hit it.
models.caveat: Scores only the first token of each option key, so in UNO all cards of one colour (red_5, red_skip, …) get the same probability and it picks among them arbitrarily.

models.name: tiny-jev-0.6b
models.params_source: serve.py count of TinyJevModel -> servers/logs/tiny-jev-0.6b.params.json (Qwen3-0.6B stack + 1,025-parameter head; matches the card's 596M)
models.deploy_notes: bf16 as shipped. Their noul API takes no criteria, so noul criteria are not shown to the model. 4096-token context enforced as 422 instead of their silent truncation; no item hit it. Very strong on easy/original (48/48, 56/72), weak on hard (29/111).

models.name: openjev-nli-0.8b
models.params_source: serve.py count of the Qwen3_5ForSequenceClassification the authors' loader holds: text 752,393,024 + NLI head 3,072 + unused vision tower 100,592,896
models.deploy_notes: LIKELY CONTAMINATED on JevBench public items: fine-tuned from 'qwen3.5-0.8b-nli-v2s-jev', whose data mix ('jevfmt') trains on the JevBench public items x8 unless --no-jevbench (used only for v3/v4/v5 per the authors). NLI cross-encoder: one forward pass per option; answers independent of option order. bf16. 4096 tokens per (state, option) pair enforced as 422.
models.caveat: Likely trained on the JevBench public items: its parent checkpoint (…-nli-v2s-jev) comes from a data mix that includes them, so its JevBench score is probably not a clean measure.

models.name: simplejev-0.8b
models.params_source: launcher probe servers/logs/simplejev-0.8b.params.json (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration incl. the 100.6M vision tower; text-only 752,393,024)
models.deploy_notes: Untrained baseline (prompt policy on stock Qwen3.5-0.8B), fp32, same command as the JevBench v1.4 'SimpleJev' entry but on CUDA; easy tier 0.875 matches that entry. The wrapper adds ~330 tokens + ~26 per option; 3 failures are the authors' 422s on the longest long_policy items.

models.name: decision-kai
models.params_source: param probe and serve.py agree (489 tensors); matches the authors' ARCHITECTURE.md
models.deploy_notes: Only change: the authors' ROCm-only device guard swapped for one accepting CUDA (falls back to upstream ModernBERT attention). FP32, TF32 off. 1024-token hard limit for the packed input (authors' own 422, no truncation); the 44 failures exceed it (1055-3853 tokens). Accuracy on the 187 answered items 0.610.

models.name: decision-lex
models.params_source: param probe: 489 tensors (card: 571,909,635)
models.deploy_notes: Same setup as decision-kai (English specialist). 44 over-long items fail with 422. Accuracy on the 187 answered items 0.604.

models.name: julia-1
models.params_source: serve.py count of JuliaDecisionModel (card: 144.3M)
models.deploy_notes: CUDA BF16 autocast (package default). Strict limits refused with 422: 2-20 options, each option at most 48 tokens, instructions + options at most 512, packed total at most 8192. The model sees option descriptions, not keys.
models.caveat: Its server caps one option at 48 tokens, so in UNO an over-long option description is shortened for it (least important clauses first, e.g. 'You will have N cards left.'); every other model gets the full text.

models.name: lumma-fev-0.1b
models.params_source: servers/logs/lumma-fev-0.1b.params.json (probe); shared layers (layer_sharing x2) counted once; matches model.safetensors
models.deploy_notes: Authors' server unchanged except a guard turning their silent cut of the state to 1408 tokens into HTTP 422. All 37 failures are hard items with states of 1839-3702 tokens. Accuracy on the 194 items it could take: 46.4% (hard 27/74). bf16 with an fp32 head, ~1 GB.

models.name: lumma-fev-0.6b
models.params_source: servers/logs/lumma-fev-0.6b.params.json (probe); LoRA already merged into the published weights
models.deploy_notes: Same guard as 0.1b; 8192-token state limit, over-long input gets 422. bf16, ~1.3 GB.

models.name: system-one-gemma
models.params_source: serve.py and probe agree: 268,098,176 gemma-3-270m + 3,797,632 unmerged LoRA/score head + 640 unused original score head
models.deploy_notes: Authors' format, one sequence per option, last-token scalar, fp32, T=2.35. The authors cut the state to 256 (app.py) or 384 tokens (infer.py); here nothing is cut (422 beyond 8192), so the model runs on inputs longer than it was trained on. noul = options yes/no; score = the levels as options. Cost grows with options x state length.

Limits: 1024 tokens total; question + options at most 256; each option at most 48 tokens; laya_guard returns 422 instead of silent cutting. 37 failures over 1024 tokens; accuracy on the 194 answered items 0.624. max_options=5 is practical (256-token head).
models.caveat: Its server caps one option at 48 tokens, so in UNO an over-long option description is shortened for it (least important clauses first, e.g. 'You will have N cards left.'); every other model gets the full text.

The wrapper switches on the authors' strict=True (422 above 8192 instead of silent truncation). fp32 SDPA, T=1.516. torch 2.13 instead of the locked 2.8 (aarch64). Repo HEAD api.py/data.py differ from the training-time hashes in provenance.json (single squashed commit).

models.name: von
models.params_source: servers/logs/von.params.json (probe): 394,781,696 ModernBERT-large + 528,385 scorer MLP
models.deploy_notes: Matches the authors' claimed per-tier numbers. The guard adds 422 above the 8192 window. Option-order independent; all options share one packed sequence. Its temperature map was fitted on these same 231 JevBench items, so Brier and ECE are in-sample (argmax unaffected). fp32.
models.caveat: Its temperature calibration was fitted on these same 231 items, so its Brier and ECE are in-sample (accuracy is unaffected).

models.name: tasksource-jev-nano

models.name: laya-multilingual
models.params_source: serve.py count of the loaded model (card: 322M)
models.deploy_notes: max_len=8192 (card setting for long inputs). Limits: question + options at most 256; each option at most 48 tokens (about 4% of UNO template-B move requests have a longer option and get 422). Uncalibrated. The adapter refuses to start if laya falls back to CPU; results are the GPU rerun.
models.caveat: Its server caps one option at 48 tokens, so in UNO an over-long option description is shortened for it (least important clauses first, e.g. 'You will have N cards left.'); every other model gets the full text.

models.name: jevembed-0.6b
models.params_source: servers/logs/jevembed-0.6b.params.json (probe; SentenceTransformer, merged LoRA)
models.deploy_notes: Bi-encoder, each text limited to 1024 tokens. Our yaml keeps the authors' prompts and scoring but sets overflow_policy: error (422), so 41 long hard items fail; acc on the 190 valid items 0.642. Authors' exact truncate@1024: acc 0.5844 / hard 0.3694; error@32768: 0.5714 / 0.3423. Returns 429 beyond 4 concurrent requests (authors' default).
